pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Useful error message when two assets have the save UUID
pr_body:
# Objective
Fixes #2610 and #3731

## Solution

Added check for TYPE_UUID duplication in  `register_asset_type` with an error message
pr_comments: I think we should check whether the two assets actually have different types, as registration would ideally be idempotent.

> I think we should check whether the two assets actually have different types, as registration would ideally be idempotent.

This will be handled by #3560

issue_context.title: unwrap() fails in an AssetServer::update_asset_storage() if two assets are registered with the same uuid
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

The unwrap here:
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/43d99bb583866c1adb4aa88f19b88637df0a7f33/crates/bevy_asset/src/asset_server.rs#L501-L503

fails when two asset types are registered with the same UUID, the stack trace of the crash isn't assisting a lot in understanding why that might happen. I would like it If it could be documented.
comments:
My first impression is that this could be improved by changing the unwrap to an `.expect` with a useful error message. It looks like this should fail if the [`downcast_ref`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/any/trait.Any.html#method.downcast_ref) results in the boxed value not actually being of the appropriate type.

In this case, that means a failure in type registration: I suspect you'll get a panic at the same place if you fail to register it at all.

@TheRawMeatball points out that this core issue of duplicate type registration can (and should) first be caught at the `add_asset` call [here](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/b724a0f586e6186f2a6ce4eb7903be0e340649e9/crates/bevy_asset/src/assets.rs). Following the chain, it looks like this is actually an issue with `register_type`, which should fail around [here](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/19799b8d94de9057cbf2fba3077cf9cd0f26a9a4/crates/bevy_reflect/src/type_registry.rs#L41) if a duplicate exists. IMO this should be a `Result`, but I'm not sure that plays nice with our builder pattern API for App...

 That said, even improving the panic with a real error message would help folks debug.

review_comments: rather than grab a read lock and then a write lock immediately after, I think we should just grab a single write lock and reuse it across both cases (especially given that the "read only" case is the "unexpected" / "uncommon" case).
